newsitem.title: USA: N. Carolina prosecutor seeks building fund audit.
newsitem.headline: N. Carolina prosecutor seeks building fund audit.

text.p: North Carolina's Wake County District Attorney has asked the state auditor to review the way lawmakers spent a $21.3 million surplus in the state's Repair and Renovation Reserve, according to published reports.
Wake District Attorney Colon Willoughby Jr. said in a June 6 letter to state Auditor Ralph Campbell that he did not feel it was appropriate to request a criminal investigation "at this time."
"Nevertheless there is cause for concern regarding the way these substantial sums of money have been handled," Willoughby said in the letter.
The surplus, which was administered by the Office of State Budget and Management, was supposed to be used for repairing and renovating state buildings.
Willoughby said the John Locke Foundation, a conservative Raliegh think tank, provided him with documents about the way the money was used.

According to the documents, House Speaker Harold Brubaker, R-Asheboro, and Senate Leader Marc Basnight, D-Manteo, each got $9.7 million from the surplus, which they divided among their members for projects in the members' districts.

Some of the money went to organizations that included drug and domestic violence treatment centers and a senior citizens' group. The Wilmington Star-News said $85,000 went to the Institute of Political Leaadership in Wrightsville Beach, which trains politicians, while $20,000 went to a candidate who ran unsuccessfully for a House seat in November.

"It appears to me from these documents that millions of dollars may have been disbursed outside the procedures mandated by statute and without the documentation required," Willoughby wrote in his letter to the auditor.
The auditor said his staff had received numerous inquiries about the expenditures and would review them.
